scope: STRUCTURE FOUND: the entity modes are a PIPELINE - modes 3 and 4 accumulate values into stream scratch fields, and modes 1/8 commit them into the entity struct

mode_3_and_4_are_accumulators.mode 3 @0x6717A1: reads 11 bits and stores them at [esi+0x24]
mode_3_and_4_are_accumulators.mode 4 @0x6717B5: reads one -97 value and stores it at [esi+0x28]

mode_1_is_a_commit.0x6718A8: cl = [0x7859559]          <- the entity-id width computed by the list parser
mode_1_is_a_commit.0x6718C5: eax = word [eax*2 + 0x7859358]   <- index into the entity id array
mode_1_is_a_commit.0x6718CD: [edi+0x18] = eax         <- entity field at +0x18 (a reference to another entity)

mode_8_is_a_partial_commit.difference_from_mode_1: no [edi+0x18] write, i.e. no cross-entity reference

why_this_is_a_structural_insight: the delta is NOT a field loop and NOT a single field - it is a SEQUENCE of mode-coded operations
modes 3 and 4 write into stream scratch fields (+0x24, +0x28)
modes 1 and 8 take those scratch values and write them into the entity struct at +0x10, +8, +0x30 and (mode 1 only) +0x18
so a real entity update looks like: [mode 3: set scratch A][mode 4: set scratch B][mode 1: commit A and B into the entity]
and that explains why single-mode bodies changed nothing visible: they set scratch values that were never committed
the_concrete_target_now: emit a three-operation delta: mode 3 (11-bit value), mode 4 (-97 value), mode 1 (commit)
then the entity struct at [edi+0x10], [+8] and [+0x30] receives real values
+0x10 and +8 are the first two fields of the 0x58-byte entity state, which is where a position would live
